supported.meaning: The exact declared scope has a dispatchable implementation and complete public conformance evidence.
supported.claimRule: Capabilities also require metadata, executor, input/output schemas, conformance fixture, and QA assertions.

experimental.meaning: A bounded path or contract exists but stability, coverage, or required evidence is incomplete.
experimental.claimRule: Must be labeled experimental at every API, CLI, and documentation boundary; capability rows still require metadata, executor, input/output schemas, conformance fixture, and QA assertions.

manual.meaning: The result depends on an explicit trusted human or external-runtime gate.
manual.claimRule: Must remain unresolved until recorded manual evidence exists and can never become an automatic pass.

unsupported.meaning: The current product does not accept or promise the item.
unsupported.claimRule: Reject or report unavailable before output mutation; never silently flatten or infer a fallback.

Parses the bounded PowerPoint transcript and grants only the exact ordered-deck-open-save-reopen receipt when readable slide order and text converge.
Builds the fixed public-synthetic candidate, enforces explicit trust and CI exclusion, preserves the source, and writes ignored local evidence only after every output validates.
Uses only PowerPoint's static object model with absolute files to open, export, save, close, reopen, and inventory the exact ordered candidate.
Covers deterministic candidate construction, exact readable transcript acceptance, semantic drift and slide-loss rejection, static least-privilege checks, explicit trust, and CI refusal.
Pure byte inspector reports only the fixed readable fraction transition and narrow observed topology, with no human fact, gate verdict, receipt, delivery, or support authority.

Trusted-local CI-refusing recorder pins the exact candidate, CandidateBuildRecord, derivative, source, and slide relation and stores explicit operator attestation separately in ignored feature-level evidence.
Rejects alternate candidates, collateral or unknown-part changes, unknown OMML nodes, record drift, unsafe byte containers, missing explicit trust/attestation, and authority confusion.
